$comment: The map of interop points: every place where two implementations of the decentralized trust graph can meet. Not a ladder; points have no order. Each point names its origin. Points marked proposed were suggested by one project and become accepted when a maintainer merges the change.

layers.title: Identity
layers.asks: Who is this, and can the other side resolve and trust the identifier?

layers.title: Credentials
layers.asks: Can a statement issued in one app be verified in another?

layers.title: Ceremony
layers.asks: Can two people on two apps become connected at all?

layers.title: Wire and carriers
layers.asks: Can a sealed message travel from one app to the other?

layers.title: Documents
layers.asks: Does the other side read what arrives?

layers.title: Messaging
layers.asks: Can two connected people talk across apps?

layers.title: Membership
layers.asks: Who says someone belongs, and can another app read it?

layers.title: Shared state
layers.asks: Can several apps hold the same group data?

layers.title: Keys
layers.asks: Can implementations share group keys and recover from a captured device?

layers.title: Devices
layers.asks: What is a person with several devices, and what survives a restore?

layers.title: Trust networks and registries
layers.asks: How do communities recognise one another?

layers.title: Conformance
layers.asks: How do we know a claim holds?

layers.title: Building together
layers.asks: How do the teams and their agents work across codebases?

points.title: Identifier resolution across apps
points.asks: Each side resolves the other's DID method and finds its keys.

points.title: Writes without web access
points.asks: What a write is when no host is reachable, and whether it counts afterwards.
points.origin: Weave deck, Level 0 question: is web access necessary and sufficient

points.title: Relationship credential exchange
points.asks: A relationship credential issued in one app is verified in another.

points.title: App change with credentials
points.asks: A person moves to another app and keeps relationship and membership credentials.

points.title: Contact ceremony between apps
points.asks: Two people on different apps connect through one QR-code ceremony and both end with a credential the other app reads.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (QR-code contact ceremonies between apps); proposed as a level by rltp

points.title: Shared ceremony definitions
points.asks: Ceremonies are defined once in the DTGWG format and implemented by several apps.

points.title: Delivery through one carrier
points.asks: Two apps reach each other through the same mediator or relay over TSP.

points.title: Delivery across carriers
points.asks: Two parties at different mediators or relays still reach each other.

points.title: Common document framework
points.asks: Wire artifacts are Trust Task documents with type URI, schema and proof the other side can check.

points.title: Error and status answers
points.asks: A receiver that cannot process a document answers in a form the sender reads.

points.title: Direct message between apps
points.asks: Two connected people on two different apps exchange a message each way, as a document both read.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (messaging across apps); proposed as a level by rltp

points.title: Deniable messages
points.asks: A message between two people carries no proof a third party can verify.

points.title: Membership statement another app reads
points.asks: A community states who belongs in a form a wallet or another app holds and verifies.

points.title: One membership, several apps
points.asks: One membership opens several apps.

points.title: Sub-groups with their own credentials
points.asks: A sub-group issues credentials of its own.

points.title: Who decides what the group is
points.asks: Owner, committer race, steward or signed log: each model named as a profile so that groups of different models can still recognise each other.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (how groups hold their own truth across apps, outliving founders); rltp

points.title: Same group in two apps
points.asks: Several apps read and write the same encrypted shared state of one community.
points.origin: Weave deck, Level 2a; one-pager (being in the same group in two different apps)

points.title: History for newcomers
points.asks: A member admitted later reads what the group wrote before, as far as the group allows.

points.title: Group key agreement at the boundary
points.asks: Implementations with different internal key worlds share group keys through one agreement (MLS) where they meet.

points.title: Recovery after a captured device
points.asks: Removing a device ends its access to future group content on every app.

points.title: Several devices, one person
points.asks: A person's devices act for the same person toward other apps, and a lost or restored device does not break the relationship.

points.title: Registry lookup
points.asks: Two communities recognise each other through a registry.

points.title: Networks of communities
points.asks: Three or more communities in a trust network.

points.title: Interop with traditional tools
points.asks: A group governed in the trust substrate is used by a conventional tool (calendar, forum, folder) that only asks who belongs.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (how decentralized tools interoperate with traditional ones)

points.title: Wire conformance
points.asks: The TSP implementation passes the shared conformance suite.

points.title: Document conformance
points.asks: Document types are exercised by shared byte-exact vectors and a shared runner.
points.origin: Trust Tasks task force; Weave one-pager (online test and compliance harness)

points.title: Consistent user interfaces
points.asks: The same ceremony or relationship class is shown with the same words and warnings across apps.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (consistency across different user interfaces)

points.title: Agents across codebases
points.asks: Coding agents of different teams exchange findings and vectors through an end-to-end encrypted channel.

statusWords.potential: compiled from public sources: the project appears to work on this point; not confirmed by the project
statusWords.runs: code or a live service another project can exercise today
statusWords.vectors: byte-exact test vectors published, not yet exercised against another implementation
statusWords.open: the project knows the gap and says so
statusWords.n/a: the project does not aim at this point, with a reason
